experiment_name: Alkylation of Ethyl Acetoacetate with Bis(4-fluorophenyl)methylene Chloride
experiment_description: Alkylation of an active methylene compound using Sodium Hydride and a phase transfer catalyst. Note: Ethyl Acetoacetate is used as the substrate in place of Diethyl Acetamidomalonate due to library availability. Required instruments: HeatingPlate, RotaryEvaporator, LiquidChromatograph. Required reagents: SodiumHydride, Bis4FluorophenylMethyleneChloride, TetraNButylammoniumIodide.

procedure.description: Retrieve SodiumHydride, EthylAcetoacetate, Bis4FluorophenylMethyleneChloride, TetraNButylammoniumIodide, Dimethylformamide, EthylAcetate, Hexane, Acetonitrile, and SodiumChloride from ReagentCabinet and place them in the FumeHood.
procedure.safety_notes: Wear gloves and safety goggles. Handle Sodium Hydride with extreme care.

procedure.description: Weigh SodiumHydride and TetraNButylammoniumIodide using ElectronicScale. Measure EthylAcetoacetate, Bis4FluorophenylMethyleneChloride, and Dimethylformamide using Pipette.
procedure.safety_notes: Perform all weighing and measuring of hazardous reagents inside the FumeHood.

procedure.description: In a RoundBottomFlask, dissolve EthylAcetoacetate in Dimethylformamide. Carefully add SodiumHydride in small portions. Stir at room temperature for 1 hour using HeatingPlate (stirring function only).
procedure.safety_notes: Hydrogen gas will evolve. Ensure FumeHood ventilation is active. Do not seal the flask tightly.

procedure.description: Add Bis4FluorophenylMethyleneChloride and TetraNButylammoniumIodide to the reaction mixture.
procedure.safety_notes: Add reagents slowly to avoid sudden exotherms.

procedure.description: Attach GrahamCondenser to the flask. Heat the mixture to 50°C for 16 hours, then increase to 80°C for another 16 hours. Monitor temperature with Thermometer.
procedure.safety_notes: Ensure cooling water is flowing through the condenser. Monitor for overheating.

procedure.description: Cool the reaction mixture to room temperature. Carefully quench excess SodiumHydride by adding Water dropwise.
procedure.safety_notes: Quenching NaH is exothermic and releases hydrogen. Add water very slowly.

procedure.description: Transfer mixture to SeparatoryFunnel. Extract with EthylAcetate and Hexane. Wash organic layer with water and SodiumChloride solution (brine).
procedure.safety_notes: Vent SeparatoryFunnel frequently to release pressure.

procedure.description: Collect the organic layer and remove solvents using the RotaryEvaporator.
procedure.safety_notes: Ensure proper vacuum and cooling to trap solvents.

procedure.description: Dissolve a small sample of the residue in Acetonitrile in a VolumetricFlask and analyze using the LiquidChromatograph.
procedure.safety_notes: Dispose of chemical waste in appropriate containers.

safety_warnings: Sodium Hydride is water-reactive and pyrophoric; handle under inert conditions if possible and quench with extreme caution.
Dimethylformamide is toxic and easily absorbed through skin; wear appropriate chemical resistant gloves.
Bis(4-fluorophenyl)methylene chloride is a halogenated alkylating agent; avoid all contact.
notes: Ethyl Acetoacetate is used as the active methylene compound. Reaction times are based on the reference protocol for similar substrates.
